title: y says /y/
parentNote: y says /y/ — the sound at the front of yak, yes, yell, yarn and yellow. It is a quick sound, so clip it short: say it as the start of yak rather than as yuh, or your child will read yes as yuh-es and hear three beats in a two-beat word. Today y is only ever at the front of a word, and that is the whole job for now. A y on the end of a word does something else entirely, and it turns up much later in the course with a day of its own, so if your child spots one in the wild there is nothing to explain yet — just read it for them and move on. The other slip to expect is y and w getting swapped, because both are made with the mouth moving rather than stopping. yell and well are in here side by side on purpose.

activities.mouthCue: The middle of your tongue jumps up to the roof of your mouth and springs straight off again.
activities.prompt: A new letter, and it is a quick one. Do not hold it: y.
Three sounds that slip out of your mouth. Find the new one.
Careful, this one is close. Two of these are a long smile. Today's is a quick jump.
Three sounds, and the new one is at the front. Keep it short.
Two l letters on the end, but they are one sound. So this is three sounds, not four.
A bossy r in the middle. The y is still quick and the ar is still long.
The long one. Two beats, and it stops on a team that says oh.
The same ending on all three. Everything you need is in the first sound.
Now they all start with the new sound, so listen right to the end.
This one is hard. Two of them start with a y, and two of them end with a d.

activities.text: He did yell at me to go out to the yard and get the yellow yarn.
Is the yak in the yard, or did it get out and go up the hill?
Yes, we did see it, and then it did eat a yam and did yell at us.

activities.title: The yak in the yard
activities.prompt: Read the story one line at a time. Tap any word you want to hear again.
lines: A yak did get out, and it did stand in the yard and yell.
Mum did yelp. Dad did shout. Meg did just stand still.
I did get a big yam and did wave it at the yak.
It did not want the yam. It did want the yellow yarn on the step.
It did grab the yarn and did munch and munch and munch.
Then it did run off, and the long yellow string did run with it.
We did trail up the hill, and the yarn did stop at a big oak.
Up in the oak sat a nest, and that nest is yellow and soft and big.
So the yak did not rob us. It did lend the yarn to a crow.
Yes, we did let it stay, and it did not yell at us till sun up.
